newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Three bids accepted in Portugal's Tabaqueira selloff.
newsitem.headline: Three bids accepted in Portugal's Tabaqueira selloff.

text.p: The panel presiding over the privatisation of Portuguese cigarette manufacturer Tabaqueira has accepted three bids, its president Jose Martins de Sa said on Tuesday.

The three bidding groups are: Portugal's Jorge de Mello industrial group, in partnership with U.S. tobacco company Philip Morris, via Portuguese holding PMM-Philip Morris e Mello; Seita of France; and Portugal's Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos, in partnership with Spain's Tabacalera.
The sealed bids for a 65 percent stake in Tabaqueira were delivered to the offices of the Inspectorate General of Finance in Lisbon on Monday evening.
The values of the bids were due to be formally announced in a public ceremony later.

The Socialist government, which plans to sell the stake by public competition at a minimum price of 4,650 escudos ($30) per share, has said it expected to raise more than 32 billion escudos ($207 million) from the sale.
Tabaqueira has a dominant share of the Portuguese tobacco market.
